literal: Earlier the Shizu Emperor had ordered that Guang's second daughter be taken as crown princess; in the first year of Tiantong she was invested as empress.
idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Wucheng had ordered Guang's second daughter taken as crown princess; in the first year of Tiantong she was invested empress.

literal: That year Guang was transferred to Grand General.
idiomatic: That year Guang was made grand general.

literal: In the sixth month of the third year, on his father's death he left office; that same month an edict recalled Guang and his younger brother Xian to their former posts.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year he left office upon his father's death; that same month an edict recalled Guang and his younger brother Xian to their former posts.

literal: In autumn he was made Grand Preceptor, succeeded to the title Prince of Xianyang, and also succeeded as First Chief of the Tribal Register; separately he was enfeoffed Duke of Wude Commandery, his revenue was transferred to Zhao Province, and he was promoted to Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: In autumn he was made grand preceptor, succeeded to the title prince of Xianyang and to the office of first chief of the tribal register, was separately enfeoffed duke of Wude Commandery with revenue transferred to Zhao Province, and was promoted to grand tutor.

literal: In the twelfth month Zhou sent generals to besiege Luoyang and cut off its grain routes.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhou sent generals to besiege Luoyang and choke off its grain routes.

literal: In the first month of the first year of Wuping an edict ordered Guang to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry against them.
idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Wuping an edict ordered Guang to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry against them.

literal: The army halted at Dinglong; Zhou generals Zhangye Duke Yuwen Jie, Governor of Zhong Province Liang Shiyan, and Kaifu Director of Water Affairs Liang Jingxing and others again encamped at the Lulu crossroads. Guang donned armor and took up sharp weapons, leading from the front; blades had barely crossed when Jie's force broke completely — more than two thousand heads were taken.
idiomatic: The army halted at Dinglong. Zhou generals Zhangye Duke Yuwen Jie, Zhong Province governor Liang Shiyan, and Kaifu director of water affairs Liang Jingxing and others had again encamped at the Lulu crossroads. Guang donned armor, seized a sharp blade, and led from the front; blades had barely crossed when Jie's men broke completely — more than two thousand heads were taken.

literal: He pressed on to Yiyang and faced Zhou Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and Duke of Shen Baba Xianjing in stalemate for ten ten-day periods.
idiomatic: He pressed on to Yiyang and faced Zhou Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and Duke of Shen Baba Xianjing in stalemate for a hundred days.

literal: Guang built and garrisoned the two fortresses Tongguan and Fenghua to open the road to Yiyang.
idiomatic: Guang built and garrisoned the fortresses Tongguan and Fenghua to keep the road to Yiyang open.

literal: On the return march, when the army reached Anye, Xian and the others numbered fifty thousand men and still trailed behind; Guang unleashed cavalry against them and Xian's force broke completely. He captured their Kaifu Yuwen Ying, Supervisor Yueqin Shiliang, Han Yan, and others, and took more than three hundred heads besides.
idiomatic: On the return march, when the army reached Anye, Xian's force — fifty thousand strong — still trailed behind. Guang unleashed cavalry and Xian's men broke completely. He captured their Kaifu Yuwen Ying, supervisor Yueqin Shiliang, Han Yan, and others, and took more than three hundred heads besides.

literal: Xian then ordered Jie and his grand general Central Duke Liang Luodu, together with Jingxing, Shiyan, and others, to post thirty thousand infantry and cavalry at the Lulu pass and block the vital route.
idiomatic: Xian then ordered Jie and his grand general Central Duke Liang Luodu, together with Jingxing, Shiyan, and others, to post thirty thousand infantry and cavalry at the Lulu pass and cut the vital route.

literal: Guang joined Han Guisun, Huyan Zu, Wang Xian, and others in a combined attack and routed them completely, beheading Jingxing and taking a thousand horses.
idiomatic: Guang joined Han Guisun, Huyan Zu, Wang Xian, and others in a combined attack and routed them completely, beheading Jingxing and taking a thousand horses.

literal: An edict additionally made him Right Chancellor and Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: An edict additionally made him right chancellor and governor of Bing Province.

literal: That winter Guang again led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to build the two fortresses Huagu and Longmen at Yubi, facing Xian, Xianjing, and the others in stalemate; Xian and the rest did not dare move.
idiomatic: That winter Guang again led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to build the fortresses Huagu and Longmen at Yubi and faced Xian, Xianjing, and the others in stalemate; Xian's men did not dare move.

literal: Guang then pressed on to besiege Dingyang and also built the fortress Nanchen.
idiomatic: Guang then pressed on to besiege Dingyang and also built the fortress Nanchen.

literal: A province was established to press them; more than ten thousand households of barbarians and Chinese alike came over and submitted.
idiomatic: A province was established to press them, and more than ten thousand households of barbarians and Chinese alike came over and submitted.

literal: In the second year he led troops to build thirteen garrison fortresses, including Pinglong, Weiqi, and Tongrong.
idiomatic: In the second year he led troops to build thirteen garrison fortresses, including Pinglong, Weiqi, and Tongrong.

literal: Zhou pillar lord Duke of Baohan Putun Wei, pillar lord Wei Xiaokuan, and others with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry came to press Pinglong; they fought Guang north of the Fen River and Guang routed them completely, capturing and slaying more than a thousand.
idiomatic: Zhou pillar lords Duke of Baohan Putun Wei and Wei Xiaokuan and others, with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry, came to press Pinglong. They fought Guang north of the Fen River; Guang routed them completely, capturing and slaying more than a thousand.

literal: He was again enfeoffed Duke of Zhongshan Commandery, with a fief increased by one thousand households.
idiomatic: He was again enfeoffed duke of Zhongshan Commandery, with a fief increased by one thousand households.

literal: When the army returned, an edict again ordered him to lead fifty thousand infantry and cavalry out by the Pingyang route to attack the garrison fortresses of Yaoqiang and Baiting; both were taken. Nine fortress commanders of Yitong and grand governor rank were captured, and several thousand captives were taken.
idiomatic: When the army returned, an edict again ordered him to lead fifty thousand infantry and cavalry out by the Pingyang route against the garrison fortresses of Yaoqiang and Baiting; both fell. Nine fortress commanders of Yitong and grand governor rank were captured, along with several thousand prisoners.

literal: He was separately enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.
idiomatic: He was separately enfeoffed duke of Changle Commandery.

literal: That month Zhou sent its pillar lord Heggan Guanglue to besiege Yiyang.
idiomatic: That month Zhou sent its pillar lord Heggan Guanglue to besiege Yiyang.

literal: Guang led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to the relief; a great battle was fought below the walls, and he then took four Zhou garrisons including Jian'an, capturing more than a thousand prisoners before returning.
idiomatic: Guang led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to the relief. A great battle was fought below the walls; he then took four Zhou garrisons including Jian'an and captured more than a thousand prisoners before returning.

literal: Before the army reached Ye, an edict ordered the troops dismissed at once.
idiomatic: Before the army reached Ye, an edict ordered the troops dismissed at once.

literal: Guang thought that many soldiers had earned merit and had not yet been rewarded and comforted; if they were dismissed immediately, imperial favor would not reach them. He therefore secretly sent a memorial asking that an envoy be sent to proclaim the edict while the army continued to advance.
idiomatic: Guang thought many soldiers had earned merit without yet receiving reward or comfort; if they were dismissed immediately, imperial favor would never reach them. He secretly sent a memorial asking that an envoy proclaim the edict while the army continued to advance.

literal: The court's envoy was slow in coming; when the army returned and was nearing Zimo, Guang still encamped and waited for the envoy.
idiomatic: The court's envoy was slow in coming. When the army returned and was nearing Zimo, Guang still encamped and waited for the envoy.

literal: When the emperor heard that Guang's army camp was already pressing close, he was deeply displeased and urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang for an audience; only then were the troops rewarded and dismissed.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Guang's army camp was already pressing close, he was deeply displeased and urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang for an audience; only then were the troops rewarded and dismissed.

literal: Guang was made Left Chancellor and separately enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe Commandery.
idiomatic: Guang was made left chancellor and separately enfeoffed duke of Qinghe Commandery.

literal: When Guang entered court he would often sit behind the hanging curtain in the hall of audience.
idiomatic: When Guang entered court he would often sit behind the hanging curtain in the hall of audience.

literal: Zu Ting did not know and rode his horse past in front of him.
idiomatic: Zu Ting did not know and rode past in front of him.

literal: Guang was angry and said to others, "This man dares behave so!
idiomatic: Guang was furious and said to others, "This man dares behave so!

literal: " Later Ting was in the inner secretariat speaking in a loud, insolent voice; Guang happened to pass by, heard it, and was angry again.
idiomatic: " Later Ting was in the inner secretariat speaking in a loud, insolent voice. Guang happened to pass by, heard it, and grew angry again.

literal: Ting knew Guang's wrath and bribed one of Guang's attendants to ask, "Is the Prince angry with Xiaozheng?
idiomatic: Ting knew Guang's wrath and bribed one of Guang's attendants to ask, "Is the Prince angry with Xiaozheng?

literal: " The answer came: "Since you took power, the Prince every night sits hugging his knees and sighs, 'The blind man has entered — the state is sure to fall!
idiomatic: " The answer came: "Since you took power, the Prince every night sits hugging his knees and sighs, 'The blind man has entered — the state is sure to fall!

literal: '" Mu Tipo asked to marry Guang's concubine-born daughter; permission was refused.
idiomatic: '" Mu Tipo asked to marry Guang's concubine-born daughter; permission was refused.

literal: The emperor bestowed on Tipo fields at Jinyang; Guang said at court, "These fields since the Shenwu Emperor have always been sown with grain to feed several thousand horses against enemy raids. To give them to Tipo now — will this not cripple military affairs?
idiomatic: The emperor bestowed on Tipo fields at Jinyang. Guang said at court, "These fields since the Shenwu Emperor have always been sown with grain to feed several thousand horses against enemy raids. To give them to Tipo now — will this not cripple military affairs?

literal: " From this Zu and Mu nursed deep resentment.
idiomatic: " From this Zu and Mu nursed deep resentment.

literal: Zhou general Wei Xiaokuan, jealous of Guang's valor, composed slanderous verses and had spies leak the text at Ye: "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; Bright Moon shines on Chang'an," and also, "The high mountain needs no push to collapse; the oak needs no prop to stand straight."
idiomatic: Zhou general Wei Xiaokuan, jealous of Guang's valor, composed slanderous verses and had spies leak the text at Ye: "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; Bright Moon shines on Chang'an," and also, "The high mountain needs no push to collapse; the oak needs no prop to stand straight."

literal: Zu Ting then added to them: "The blind old husband carries a great axe on his back; the sharp-tongued old woman cannot speak.
idiomatic: Zu Ting then added to them: "The blind old husband carries a great axe on his back; the sharp-tongued old woman cannot speak.

literal: " He had children sing them in the streets.
idiomatic: " He had children sing them in the streets.

literal: Tipo heard of it and told his mother Ling Xuan.
idiomatic: Tipo heard of it and told his mother Ling Xuan.

literal: Xuan took "sharp-tongued" as a reproach against herself and "blind old husband" as referring to Ting; they therefore joined in plotting and reported the verses to the emperor, saying, "The Hulü clan for generations has been great generals; Bright Moon's fame shakes the lands west of the passes, Fengle's authority reaches the Turks; a daughter is empress and sons marry princesses — the verses are truly fearsome.
idiomatic: Xuan took "sharp-tongued" as a reproach against herself and "blind old husband" as referring to Ting. They therefore joined in plotting and reported the verses to the emperor, saying, "The Hulü clan for generations has been great generals; Bright Moon's fame shakes the lands west of the passes, Fengle's authority reaches the Turks; a daughter is empress and sons marry princesses — the verses are truly fearsome.

literal: " The emperor asked Han Changluan; Changluan said it could not be done, and the matter rested.
idiomatic: " The emperor asked Han Changluan; Changluan said it could not be done, and the matter rested.

literal: Zu Ting again saw the emperor and asked for a private audience; only He Hongzhen was at his side.
idiomatic: Zu Ting again saw the emperor and asked for a private audience; only He Hongzhen was at his side.

literal: The emperor said, "I received your earlier memorial and at once wished to carry it out; Changluan said there was no reason for it.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I received your earlier memorial and at once wished to carry it out; Changluan said there was no reason for it.

literal: " Before Ting could answer, Hongzhen stepped forward and said, "If there had never been such intent, that would be one thing; but once such intent exists and is not decisively carried out, what if it leaks?
idiomatic: " Before Ting could answer, Hongzhen stepped forward and said, "If there had never been such intent, that would be one thing; but once such intent exists and is not decisively carried out, what if it leaks?

literal: " The emperor said, "Hongzhen speaks rightly.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Hongzhen speaks rightly.

literal: " He still hesitated, undecided.
idiomatic: " He still hesitated, undecided.

literal: It happened that Chief Administrator of the Chancellor's Office Feng Shirang sent a secret memorial saying, "When Guang returned from the western campaign, an edict ordered the troops dismissed; Guang kept the army pressing the imperial capital, intending to commit treason, but the plot failed and stopped.
idiomatic: It happened that chief administrator of the chancellor's office Feng Shirang sent a secret memorial saying, "When Guang returned from the western campaign, an edict ordered the troops dismissed; Guang kept the army pressing the imperial capital, intending treason, but the plot failed and stopped.

literal: At home he hoards crossbows and armor; he has a thousand-odd slaves and servants; he constantly sends messengers to Fengle and Wudu, plotting back and forth in secret.
idiomatic: At home he hoards crossbows and armor and keeps a thousand-odd slaves and servants; he constantly sends messengers to Fengle and Wudu, plotting back and forth in secret.

literal: If he is not dealt with early, I fear matters may become unpredictable.
idiomatic: If he is not dealt with early, I fear matters may become unpredictable.

literal: " The memorial's words "the army pressing the imperial capital" matched the emperor's earlier suspicions; he said to He Hongzhen, "Heaven's mind is also a great sage — I earlier suspected he wished to rebel, and so it proves.
idiomatic: " The memorial's words "the army pressing the imperial capital" matched the emperor's earlier suspicions. He said to He Hongzhen, "Heaven's mind is also a great sage — I earlier suspected he wished to rebel, and so it proves.

literal: " The emperor was by nature extremely timid; fearing an immediate outbreak, he ordered Hongzhen to gallop and summon Zu Ting to tell him.
idiomatic: " The emperor was by nature extremely timid. Fearing an immediate outbreak, he ordered Hongzhen to gallop and summon Zu Ting to tell him.

literal: He also feared that if Guang were summoned he would not obey.
idiomatic: He also feared that if Guang were summoned he would not obey.

literal: Ting therefore said, "If you summon him directly, I fear he will suspect and refuse to enter.
idiomatic: Ting therefore said, "If you summon him directly, I fear he will suspect and refuse to enter.

literal: You should send an envoy to bestow a fine horse on him, saying, 'Tomorrow I shall go to the Eastern Hills for an outing; the Prince may ride this horse and come with me' — Guang will surely come to give thanks, and you can then bring him in and seize him.
idiomatic: You should send an envoy to bestow a fine horse on him, saying, 'Tomorrow I shall go to the Eastern Hills for an outing; the Prince may ride this horse and come with me' — Guang will surely come to give thanks, and you can then bring him in and seize him.

literal: " The emperor did as he said.
idiomatic: " The emperor did as he said.

literal: Before long Guang arrived; he was brought into the Cool Breeze Hall, and Liu Taozhi strangled him from behind and killed him. He was fifty-eight.
idiomatic: Before long Guang arrived. He was brought into the Cool Breeze Hall, and Liu Taozhi strangled him from behind and killed him. He was fifty-eight.

literal: Thereupon an edict was issued declaring that Guang had plotted rebellion and had now paid with his life; the rest of his household need not be investigated.
idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued declaring that Guang had plotted rebellion and had now paid with his life; the rest of his household need not be investigated.

literal: Soon another edict was issued exterminating the entire clan.
idiomatic: Soon another edict was issued exterminating the entire clan.

literal: Guang by nature spoke little, was stern and quick-tempered, strict in commanding subordinates; in drilling troops and supervising the ranks he relied solely on awe and punishment.
idiomatic: Guang by nature spoke little, was stern and quick-tempered, and strict with subordinates; in drilling troops and supervising the ranks he relied solely on awe and punishment.

literal: In corvée labor for wall-building he whipped gentlemen and was widely called brutal.
idiomatic: In corvée labor for wall-building he whipped gentlemen and was widely called brutal.

literal: From the time he first bound his hair and took up arms he never once lost discipline; neighboring enemies deeply feared him.
idiomatic: From the time he first bound his hair and took up arms he never once lost discipline, and neighboring enemies deeply feared him.

literal: His guilt was never made clear, yet in a single day he was slaughtered to extinction; court and common people alike mourned and lamented.
idiomatic: His guilt was never made clear, yet in a single day he was slaughtered to extinction; court and common people alike mourned and lamented.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou heard that Guang was dead he rejoiced greatly and proclaimed an amnesty within his borders.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou heard that Guang was dead he rejoiced greatly and proclaimed an amnesty within his borders.

literal: Later, when he entered Ye, he posthumously enfeoffed Guang as Pillar of State and Duke of Chong.
idiomatic: Later, when he entered Ye, he posthumously enfeoffed Guang as pillar of state and duke of Chong.

literal: Pointing at the edict he said, "If this man were still alive, how could I have reached Ye!"
idiomatic: Pointing at the edict he said, "If this man were still alive, how could I have reached Ye!"

literal: Guang had four sons.
idiomatic: Guang had four sons.

literal: The eldest, Wudu, rose through the posts of Special Advance, Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, Kaifu Yitong Third Rank, and Governor of Liang and Yan Provinces.
idiomatic: The eldest, Wudu, rose through the posts of special advance, grand preceptor to the crown prince, Kaifu Yitong Third Rank, and governor of Liang and Yan Provinces.

literal: Everywhere he served he showed no administrative achievement and devoted himself only to amassing wealth, plundering the common people.
idiomatic: Everywhere he served he showed no administrative achievement and devoted himself only to amassing wealth, plundering the common people.

literal: When Guang died, an envoy was sent to the province to behead him.
idiomatic: When Guang died, an envoy was sent to the province to behead him.

literal: Next was Xuda, Central Guard General and Kaifu Yitong Third Rank; he died before Guang.
idiomatic: Next was Xuda, central guard general and Kaifu Yitong Third Rank; he died before Guang.

literal: Next was Shixiong, Kaifu Yitong Third Rank.
idiomatic: Next was Shixiong, Kaifu Yitong Third Rank.

literal: Next was Hengga, acting Kaifu Yitong Third Rank.
idiomatic: Next was Hengga, acting Kaifu Yitong Third Rank.

literal: All were granted death.
idiomatic: All were granted death.

literal: Guang's youngest son Zhong, only a few years old, was spared.
idiomatic: Guang's youngest son Zhong, only a few years old, was spared.

literal: Under the Zhou dynasty he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Chong.
idiomatic: Under the Zhou dynasty he inherited the enfeoffment as duke of Chong.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as General of Fast Cavalry.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as general of fast cavalry.

literal: Xian, styled Fengle, from youth was quick-witted and especially skilled in archery; the Grand Ancestor saw him and praised him.
idiomatic: Xian, styled Fengle, was quick-witted from youth and especially skilled in archery; Gao Huan saw him and praised him.

literal: Shizong promoted him to staff officer of Kaifu.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng promoted him to staff officer of Kaifu.

literal: He was transferred to General Who Captures Barbarians and Palace Attendant, additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, advanced in enfeoffment to Viscount of Daxia County, and made Governor of Tong Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to general who captures barbarians and palace attendant, additionally made general who pacifies the west, advanced in enfeoffment to viscount of Daxia County, and made governor of Tong Province.

literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Xian's title was advanced to General Who Campaigns West and he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Xianqin County.
idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Xian's title was advanced to general who campaigns west and he was separately enfeoffed baron of Xianqin County.

literal: In the third year of Heqing he was transferred to bearer of the staff of authority and Area Commander of military affairs in the six provinces of You, An, Ping, South Camp, North Camp, and East Yan, and Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he was transferred to bearer of the staff of authority and area commander of military affairs in the six provinces of You, An, Ping, South Camp, North Camp, and East Yan, and governor of You Province.

literal: That autumn more than a hundred thousand Turks came raiding the borders of the province; Xian took overall command of the generals to resist them.
idiomatic: That autumn more than a hundred thousand Turks came raiding the borders of the province; Xian took overall command of the generals to resist them.

literal: The Turks saw that the army's bearing was very orderly and did not dare fight; they at once sent envoys seeking terms.
idiomatic: The Turks saw that the army's bearing was very orderly and did not dare fight; they at once sent envoys seeking terms.

literal: Fearing treachery, he also instructed them, saying, "Your journey this time was never a tribute mission; you changed only when you saw your chance — that is not a long-held intent.
idiomatic: Fearing treachery, he also instructed them, saying, "Your journey this time was never a tribute mission; you changed only when you saw your chance — that is not a long-held intent.

literal: If you have real sincerity, you should quickly return to your nests and send another envoy.
idiomatic: If you have real sincerity, you should quickly return to your nests and send another envoy.

literal: " Thereupon they withdrew and fled.
idiomatic: " Thereupon they withdrew and fled.

literal: In the fifth month of summer in the first year of Tiantong the Turk khan Muhan sent envoys requesting audience and tribute; Xian reported it for the first time. From then on tribute missions came every year without interruption — Xian had much to do with it.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the first year of Tiantong the Turk khan Muhan sent envoys requesting audience and tribute; Xian reported it for the first time. From then on tribute missions came every year without interruption — Xian had much to do with it.

literal: An edict additionally made him Vice Director of the Mobile Office.
idiomatic: An edict additionally made him vice director of the mobile office.

literal: Because northern barbarians repeatedly violated the frontier and unexpected trouble had to be guarded against, from Kudui Garrison eastward to the sea he followed the mountains in a winding line of more than two thousand li; within two hundred li of that stretch, wherever there was strategic ground, he either cut down mountains to build walls or blocked valleys to raise barriers, and in all established more than fifty garrison posts at intervals.
idiomatic: Because northern barbarians repeatedly violated the frontier and unexpected trouble had to be guarded against, from Kudui Garrison eastward to the sea he followed the mountains in a winding line of more than two thousand li. Within two hundred li of that stretch, wherever there was strategic ground, he either cut down mountains to build walls or blocked valleys to raise barriers, and in all established more than fifty garrison posts at intervals.

literal: He also diverted the Gaoliang River northward to join Yijing, and eastward to meet the Lu, and thereby irrigated fields.
idiomatic: He also diverted the Gaoliang River northward to join Yijing and eastward to meet the Lu, and thereby irrigated fields.

literal: Frontier stores accumulated year by year; transport costs were saved, and both public and private interests profited.
idiomatic: Frontier stores accumulated year by year, transport costs were saved, and both public and private interests profited.

literal: In the sixth month of that year, on his father's death he left office; he and his elder brother Guang were both recalled from mourning to their posts and returned to garrison Yan and Ji.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, on his father's death he left office; he and his elder brother Guang were both recalled from mourning to their posts and returned to garrison Yan and Ji.

literal: In the third year his rank was advanced to Special Advance.
idiomatic: In the third year his rank was advanced to special advance.

literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing of the Mobile Office and separately enfeoffed Marquis of Gaocheng County.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to director of the masters of writing of the mobile office and separately enfeoffed marquis of Gaocheng County.

literal: In the first year of Wuping he was additionally made General of Fast Cavalry.
idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was additionally made general of fast cavalry.

literal: At that time Guang's son Wudu was Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: At that time Guang's son Wudu was governor of Yan Province.

literal: Xian had served several emperors and was esteemed for his prudence and integrity; though he reached the utmost honor he did not pride himself on it — but now, with the whole house grown noble and powerful, he was deeply troubled.
idiomatic: Xian had served several emperors and was esteemed for his prudence and integrity; though he reached the utmost honor he did not pride himself on it — but now, with the whole house grown noble and powerful, he was deeply troubled.

literal: He therefore submitted a memorial yielding his rank, begging to be released from his offices; a gracious edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial yielding his rank, begging to be released from his offices; a gracious edict did not permit it.
